substance.name: Mushrooms

effects: A arylcyclohexylamine dissociative anaesthetic closely related to methoxetamine, ketamine, and PCP. It has seen some popularity among drug users, often being advertised as an MXE replacement after its illegalisation in many parts of the world. Anectodal reports indicate a more stimulating experience closer to those associated with PCP and PCP analogues.
substance.name: Mxm

effects: A drug derived from pyrovalerone which acts as a TRI, producing stimulating effects. The drug has been sold in a blend called "NRG-1". There is limited information on the drug's safety profile.
substance.name: Naphyrone

effects: A very common pain and fever reducer. It is also known as Aleve. Naproxen is in the same drug category as ibuprofen, which is also a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory. This drug is available in most places over the counter. Is sometimes used to reduce the body-load of certain drugs.
substance.name: Naproxen

effects: N-Ethylbuphedrone, an uncommon substituted cathinone. The drug was first being reported around 2011 but did not rise reportedly to great popularity. The drug's effects are suggested by anectodal reports to partially resemble other cathinones. The drug is a short-acting stimulant with more dopamine action than serotonin.
substance.name: Neb

effects: Nootropic compound of the racetam family. The drug is reported to enhance both GABAergic and cholinergic signaling. Long-term use is suggested to be neuroprotective. The drug is fat soluble.
substance.name: Nefiracetam

effects: Opioid agonist that is 2-3x the potency of morphine. The drug is used in a few countries medically. The drug has a rapid onset of effects due to its increased lipid solubility.
substance.name: Nicomorphine

effects: A pharmaceutical benzodiazepine with hypnotic sedative effects. The drug is reported to have high amounts of use and abuse in Malaysia.
substance.name: Nimetazepam

effects: A new research chemical benzodiazepine based off the chemical structure of nimetazepam. There is very limited information on the drug. The drug is suggested by anectodal reports to be similar to temazepam.
substance.name: Nitemazepam

effects: An analogue of dimethocaine with local anaesthetic and stimulant properties. The drug is often marketed in the research chemical scene as a cocaine replacement. There is little reported use of the drug.
substance.name: Nitracaine

effects: Hypnotic benzodiazepine that is used for short-term relief of anxiety and insomnia. The drug is reported to cause CNS depression.
substance.name: Nitrazepam

effects: Hypnotic benzodiazepine that is the triazolo analogue of Nitrazepam and about 4x more potent compared to the parent compound. It is also  dechlorinated derivative of clonazolam with roughly 1/10 potency.
substance.name: Nitrazolam

effects: Stimulant that is in the aminoindane class. The drug is structurally similar to it's 'bigger brother' 2-AI. In contrast, it reportedly has a lower potency and longer duration.
substance.name: Nm-2-ai

effects: Chloral Hydrate, a sedative drug discovered in 1832 with a history of recreational use going back to the 19th century. The drug is prescribed rarely for extreme insomnia. There is limited information on the drug's long-term effects on the body. The drug is reported to induce a intoxication comparable to alcohol or benzodiazepines.
substance.name: Noctec

effects: The drug is reported to have comman benzodiazepine effects, such as being an anti-convulsant, muscle relaxant, and having sedative-anxiolytic effects. The drug has active metabolites of diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, and clorazepate among many others which is where most of its effects come from. The drug has one of the longest lasting half-lifes in the benzodiazepine drug class.
substance.name: Nordazepam

effects: Benzodiazepine analogue that is an active metabolite to many other benzodiazepines, such as flurazepam, flutoprazepam, and midazolam.
substance.name: Norflurazepam

effects: An opioid analgesic which is the main active metabolite of tramadol. The drug is a µ full agonist and has additional affinity for δ (delta) and κ-opioid receptors.
substance.name: O-desmethyltramadol

effects: Dissociative of the arylcyclohexylamine class. Structurally related to deschloroketamine.
substance.name: O-pce

effects: Opium is a naturally occurring analgesic harvested as a latex from ripe Papaver somniferum (opium poppy) pods. The sap of the poppy plant primarily contains codeine and morphine with the amounts varying by plant, which can be made into a tea and consumed raw, or further processed.
substance.name: Opium

effects: A prescription benzodiazepine with intermediate duration and half life. A sedative and hypnotic which may cause lowered inhibitions and amnesia in higher doses.
substance.name: Oxazepam

effects: A benzodiazepine derivative that is a prodrug for desmethyldiazepam.
substance.name: Oxazolam

effects: Oxiracetam is a racetam nootropic, having a hydroxyl group being the only difference between this and piracetam. It used as a nootropic, namely for increased cognitive function. It is typically used two to three times a day. This substance is typically taken with choline and is reported to cause headaches without the addition of it.
substance.name: Oxiracetam

effects: A powerful semisynthetic opioid analgesic also known as Opana. A derivative of morphine, it is approximately ten times as potent as morphine. The drug has a low oral bioavailability and as such it is usually insufflated or taken rectally.
substance.name: Oxymorphone

effects: An anxiolytic drug related to zopiclone with reportedly no sedative or hypnotic qualities. The drug has been investigated as a possible alcohol replacement. Related in structure and effect to zopiclone and zolpidem.
substance.name: Pagoclone

effects: Dextromoramide, a rare and powerful opioid analgesic approximately three times as potent as morphine with a shorter duration. Generally only seen in the Netherlands. Reported as having strange and rapid tolerance behaviour.
substance.name: Palfium

effects: The drug is reportedly rare and there is little known about it. It is an extremely potent research chemical analogue of fentanyl. This powerful opioid is generally only dispensed as a nasal spray. It is strongly recommended to handle with extreme caution and to avoid mixing it with other depressants.
substance.name: Parafluorobutyrfentanyl

effects: The drug is reportedly rare and there is little known about it. It is an extremely potent research chemical analogue of fentanyl developed by Janssen Pharmaceutica in the 1960s. It is strongly recommended to handle with extreme caution and to avoid mixing it with other depressants.
substance.name: Parafluorofentanyl

effects: Eticyclidine (PCE) is a dissociative anesthetic that has hallucinogenic effects. It is reported to be slightly more potent than (PCP).
substance.name: Pce

effects: A stimulant of the 4-oxazolidinone class. The drug was used as a medication for ADHD and narcolepsy, but it was pulled from most markets due to liver failures among children.
substance.name: Pemoline

effects: A synthetic opioid used as an analgesic. It is only used IM and IV in the medical field and has respiratory depressant effects. It is pregnancy category C and schedule IV in the US.
substance.name: Pentazocine

effects: A potent NDRI cathinone-type stimulant with anectodal reports indicating the drugs effects not to be greatly recreational.
substance.name: Pentedrone

effects: A CNS depressant drug that is of the barbituate class. The drug is not used often used medically due to it's high overdose potential in contrast to a lesser overdose risk with benzodiazepine. The drug is used for the treatment of insomnia
substance.name: Pentobarbital

effects: A stimulant, empathogen, and substituted cathinone. It was first synthesised in the 1960s, and re-appeared on the research chemical scene in 2010. There is very little known about the pharmacology or effects of this compound.
substance.name: Pentylone

effects: Peyote is a small, spineless cactus that contains mescaline as its primary active chemical. It has a long history of use among the natives of Northern Mexico and Southwestern United States.
substance.name: Peyote

effects: Tropane derivative substance that is suggested to have around ~30% the potency of cocaine as a stimulant, while also having properties of a local anasthetic.
substance.name: Pfbt

effects: A very long-acting, potent, subtle benzodiazepine. Infamous for the calamitous experiences, many anectodal reports indicate the drugs suggestibility for redosing and reckless usage. The drug is prescribed in certain countries for epilepsy and alcohol withdrawal.
substance.name: Phenazepam

effects: Organic compound, which is the name of a class of chemicals that are known for psychoactive and/or stimulant effects. The compound is typically not used as a supplement as it is rapidly broken down into inactive compounds. The compound is found in many foods.
substance.name: Phenethylamine

effects: A rare phenethylamine stimulant related to 3-FPM. There is limited information on the drugs pharmacology and effects. It is suspected to have similar properties to structurally similar compounds. Caution is recommended to not confuse it with phenmetrazine.
substance.name: Phenetrazine

effects: Severe protracted withdrawal; dependence in weeks of daily use
substance.name: Phenibut

effects: Stimulant drug that was previously used as an appetite suppressant and has since been withdrawn from the market, due to concerns of abuse and addiction. Reportedly produces fewer negative side effects than common amphetamines. A study has reported it is slightly more effective than dextroamphetamine as a weight loss agent.
substance.name: Phenmetrazine

effects: CNS depressant that is typically used for insomnia in older patients and epliepsy in younger patients. Less commonlly used now medically due to a popular preference for benzodiazepines.
substance.name: Phenobarbital

effects: Psychostimulant of the substituted amphetamine class. The drug is used medically as an appetite suppressant.
substance.name: Phentermine

effects: An analogue of GABA that passes the brain blood barrier, which is then hydrolyzed into GABA and niacin. It is suggested GABA is the producer of an anxiolytic effect from this action. In contrast, it is suggested niacin acts as a vasodilator. Picamilon is often used in nootropic 'stacks'.
substance.name: Picamilon

effects: Benzodiazepine that is solely an anxiolytic drug that lacks the hypnotic and significant motor impairment that typical benzodiazepines do. The main metabolite of this drug is nordazepam and to a lesser effect oxazepam, which is where it is suggested to get most of its effects
substance.name: Pinazepam

effects: A rare psychedelic tryptamine related to DPT. There is little known about the effects or safety profile of this compound.
substance.name: Pipt

effects: Sedative-hypnotic medication made in the 1950's. The drug was used for treatment of short-term insomnia (two weeks).
substance.name: Placdyl

effects: An empathogen with a slow onset and strong serotonin release. This, combined with its lack of dopamine release, often leads users to dose more for the pleasurable effects which reportedly do not appear. This often leading to hospitalisations and deaths. The drug has been missold as MDMA.
Delayed onset leads to redose overdose deaths — DO NOT redose
substance.name: Pma

effects: A CNS stimulant nootropic that belongs to the racetam family of compounds. The nootropic is significantly more potent than piracetam while appearing to have a similar mechanism of action.
substance.name: Pramiracetam

effects: Benzodiazepine dervative. It is suggested to have effects typical to common benzodiazepines such as anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, sedation, and skeletal muscle relaxant. It is a prodrug for desmethyldiazepam which is suggested to be the causer of the majority, if not all of the effects to prazepam.
substance.name: Prazepam

effects: A sigma-1 receptor agonist derived structurally from PCP. It is reported to have cognitive enhancing effects as well as antidepressant effects. Studies are being conduced on its potential use in treating many nervous system diseases such as ALS and parkinsons.
substance.name: Pre-084

effects: A nootropic research chemical first synthesized in the 1970's. There is a single clinical study showing drastic improvement in mid-term memory among users, but otherwise it is severely under researched and caution should be given to any singular study. The reportedly does not have recreational value.
substance.name: Prl-8-53

effects: A rare lysergamide that is slightly less potent than LSD with a shorter duration of action.
substance.name: Pro-lad

effects: A stimulant drug which is a dopamine reuptake inhibitor related to MDPV and pyrovalerone. The drug was first developed in the 1950's and there are many reported cases of abuse for this drug.
substance.name: Prolintane

effects: A first generation antihistamine,  which possesses anticholinergic, strong sedative and antipsychotic properties. The drug was commonly used as a treatment for psychosis, and is now more typically used as a component of codeine cough syrups as an anti-nausea agent.
substance.name: Promethazine

effects: A very short-acting sedative that is usually given at the start of general anesthesia and for maintenance of the prior. This drug is extremely dangerous to use outside of medical settings If one is to use this drug outside of a medical setting, it is strongly recommended having another experienced individual in-person to monitor ones pulse and breathing among other concerns.
substance.name: Propofol

effects: The drug is an analgesic in the opioid family. It is intended for mild pain and for its antitussive effects. The drug has been taken off the market in Europe and the US due to concerns of fatal overdoses and heart arrhythmias.
substance.name: Propoxyphene

effects: The drug is a nonselective beta blocker. It is used in medication for high blood pressure, anxiety, and tremors.
substance.name: Propranolol

effects: A relatively common CNS stimulant sold over the counter in Benzedrex inhalers.
substance.name: Propylhexedrine

effects: An uncommon psychedelic stimulant phenethylamine and analogue of mescaline with reportedly similar effects. The drug is roughly 5-7 times more potent than mescaline by weight.
substance.name: Proscaline

effects: The drug is widely sold as a decongestant and is one isomer of ephedrine. The drug reportedly lacks in recreational effects. It is used in the synthesis of methcathinone and methamphetamine.
substance.name: Pseudoephedrine

effects: Psilocin is a substutued tryptamine alkaloid that is present in most psilocybin mushrooms. It is relatively unstable in solution due to the -OH group.
substance.name: Psilocin

effects: Poppy tea can be made from poppy pods, stalks, and seeds. It contains various opium alkaloids primarily including morphine, as well as codeine and among others. There is great variation in poppy tea potency and therefore doses are indicated for opioid naive users. There are many reports of overdoses due to inconsistent, unpredicable, dosing.
substance.name: Pst

effects: Stimulant of the pyrrolidinophenone class that is a higher homologue of α-PHP. Reportedly less potent and less effects.
substance.name: Pv-8

effects: An NDRI pyrovalerone derivative reported to have similar subjective effects to pyrovalerone. There is very limited information on the drug, further research is strongly recommended.
substance.name: Pyrophenidone

effects: Benzodiazepine derivate drug, Doral is prescribed for short-term treatment of insomnia and sleep maintenance. It's method of action is reportedly similar to zolpedim and zaleplon (and substitutes) when tested in animal studies.
substance.name: Quazepam

effects: The drug is prescribed in Japan for insomnia. The drug, also known as Rhythmy, is a benzodiazepine pro-drug which while inactive itself, is metabolised into the active compound in-vivo. The drug is soluble in water.
substance.name: Rilmazafone

effects: Rolicyclidine, also known as PCPy, is a dissociative with effects similar to PCP. The drug is reported to have less stimulating effects than PCP while keeping similarities with hallucinogenic and sedative effects. In this sense, it has been anecdotally reported to be more similar to opioids regarding effects, or other central nervous system depressants.
substance.name: Rolicyclidine

effects: A benzodiazepine derivative that posses the common benzodiazepine effects such as sedation, amnesia, and hypnotic effects. It has a long half life (51-103 hours) and metabolizes into an active compound (descarboxyloflazepate). The drug is commercialized in Mexico.
substance.name: Ronlax

effects: Stimulant of the phenyltropane class that acts as a SNDRI. The drug is suspected to have slightly slower onset and slightly longer duration than its parent compound cocaine. The drug is the tropane analogue of 3,4-CTMP.
substance.name: Rti-111

effects: A barbiturate derivative that is reported to have amnesic, hypnotic, and sedative properties, along with having similarties to other barbiturates. The drug is used in the treatment of epilepsy, short-term treatment for insomnia, and a preoperative medication for anaesthesia and anxiolysis for short surgical/diagnostic/therapeutic procedures.
substance.name: Secobarbital

effects: A perennial shrub with small narrow leaves and yellow flowers growing up to ~1.5 meters. The drug is known under many different names. The drug been used for shamanic purposes by indigenous people in Central America and Mexico. The drug is reported to be mainly auditory based.
substance.name: Sinicuichi

effects: Sedative-hypnotic of the nonbenzodiazepine (Z-drug) of the pyrazolopyramide class. The drug is mainly used medically for short-term insomnia.
substance.name: Sonata

effects: A synthetic analgesic drug that is roughly between 5-10x the potency of its parent drug fentanyl. The drug medically is very restricted to surgery and post-operative pain.
substance.name: Sufentanil

effects: A thiamine derivative nootropic and stimulant drug. Caution should be used as sulbutiamine reduces dopamine output over time with consistant usage.
substance.name: Sulbutiamine

effects: An opioid analgesic drug with potency roughly between tramadol and morphine. The drug has a similar pharmacological action to tramadol. The drug is an adrenergic reuptake inhibitor. The drug is reported to have a high addiction potential. There is a great potential for respiratory depression in overdose. The drug is highly recommended to not be combined with depressants and or stimulants.
substance.name: Tapentadol

effects: Temazepam's brand name is Restoril. It is a hypnotic benzodiazepine with effects similar to clonazepam. The drug is frequently prescribed as a sleep aid. There are some anectodal reports that indicate it has mild euphoria alongside the hypnotic effects.
substance.name: Temazepam

effects: An analogue of fentanyl with extremely limited information in medical literature. The drug is suspected to be less potent than similar analogues. Caution and further research is strongly recommended.
substance.name: Tetrahydrofuran-fentanyl

effects: A benzodiazepine that has anticonvulsant, anxiolytic, muscle relaxant, and slightly hypnotic properties. The drug was taken off the market in 2013 due to cutaneous toxicity and allergic reactions, among other reasons. The drug has been noted to be more euphoric than similar ones of it's type.
substance.name: Tetrazepam

effects: A pyrovalerone stimulant related to a-PVP and naphyrone. There is limited information about the drugs effects and safety profile. There is little evidence of human use of this drug.
substance.name: Th-pvp

effects: Small alkaloid which can be seen as a structurally modified version of caffeine, with similarly stimulating effects. The drug also shares anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects with caffeine.
substance.name: Theacrine

effects: Theobromine is the principal bitter alkaloid of the cacao bean. It has been used in various pharmaceutical products as a vasodilator, diuretic, and heart stimulant. Theobromine is consumed in cocoa, chocolate, and in various forms of chocolate-based foods. It is also present in small amounts in green coffee beans, tea, mate, and kola nut.
substance.name: Theobromine

effects: Barbiturate that that has a reportedly fast onset. The drug is used as for anesthesia in medical induced comas among other things.
substance.name: Thiopental

effects: A substance that is closely related to methiopopramine (MPA). Is roughly about 1/3rd the potency of amphetamine and differs from amphetmine from the phenyl ring in which it is switched with a thiophene ring.
substance.name: Thiopropamine

effects: Mu-opioid agonist activity; addiction and overdose risk
substance.name: Tianeptine

effects: A relatively rare dissociative anesthetic. The drug is pharmacologically classified as an NMDA receptor antagonist. It is related to other anesthetics in this family such as ketamine and phencyclidine (PCP). The drug has been used to cut ketamine, in which case it may cause additional nausea. In veterinary practice it is mixed with zolazolam which is a potent anaesthetic, at a 1:1 ratio.
substance.name: Tiletamine

effects: Synthetic opioid used mainly for the treatment of moderate to severe pain. In some countries it's mixed with naloxone to lower the abuse liability. Roughly 0.2 - 1 on the potency scale to morphine. (20mg of morphine to 100mg tilidine)
substance.name: Tilidine

effects: Trimethoxyamphetamine-2, a psychedelic amphetamine and stimulant first synthesised by Alexander Shulgin. An uncommon compound of similar activity to other psychedelic amphetamines. There is a short reported history of human use.
substance.name: Tma-2

effects: A rarely psychedelic amphetamine and mescaline analogue. First synthesised by Alexander Shulgin, who described it as  "one of the most rewarding and pleasurable of the methoxylated amphetamines."
substance.name: Tma-6

effects: Analogue of GABA and the 4-methyl analogue of phenibut. The drug is reported to have similar effects to phenibut and GABA, the drug acts on GABA(B).
substance.name: Tolibut

effects: A novel antidepressant of the SARI class, a serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor. The drug is used medically to treat depressive and anxiety disorders and symptoms. It is reported to have anxiolytic and hypnotic effects.
substance.name: Trazodone

effects: An uncommon and very short-acting benzodiazepine. Sedating and hypnotic and may induce amnesia and lowered inhibitions at higher doses.
substance.name: Triazolam

effects: A stimulant and dopamine reuptake inhibitor developed in the 1970's, it is frequently used in scientific research but has seen little usage outside of the lab. The drug is reported to have similar effects to cocaine, though reportedly much longer lasting action without local anaesthetic effects. The drug is suspected to be painful to insufflate.
substance.name: Troparil

effects: Truffles (magic truffles, sclerotium) are the thickened root sections of psilocybin mushrooms. Like psilocybin mushrooms, truffles contain the psychoactive chemicals psilocybin and psilocin.
substance.name: Truffles

effects: Brand name of a combination drug of two barbiturate salts (secobarbital and amobarbital) in equal amounts. It was introduced in the late 1940's.
substance.name: Tuinal

effects: A substance that is an analogue of U-47700 yet doesn't share much with it. Reading this reddit post has been recommended by TripSit staff. https://www.reddit.com/r/researchchemicals/comments/5gbo3e/u49900_experiment_and_warning/
substance.name: U-49900

effects: A very potent opioid that it reported to have κ-opioid action. Due to this action, it is suspected to have dysphoric and auditory hallucination effects. The drug is an analogue of U-47700.
substance.name: U-51754

effects: Opioid that is a higher homologue of butyrfentanyl with a greatly reduced potency.
substance.name: Valerylfentanyl

effects: A medication originally developed to lower blood pressure and now is widely used to treat erectile dysfunction in males. The drug is not recommended to be mixed with any other drugs that lower blood pressure. It is recommended to contact emergancy services if an erection under the substance lasts longer than 4 hours.
substance.name: Viagra

effects: NRI that was used as an antidepressant in some European countries, and now is used in the United States for ADHD. The drug has a pronouced stimulant effect similar to amphetamines without any reported signs of dependence.
substance.name: Viloxazine

effects: Also known as lisdexamphetamine, the drug is a CNS stimulant often prescribed for ADHD, narcolepsy, and obesity. It is a pro-drug for dextroamphetamine, and functions as a method for providing extended-release stimulation. The drug is sometimes medically prescribed alongside an SSRI for depression.
substance.name: Vyvanse

effects: A potent opioid that is 5.4x more potent than morphine. The drug has a distinct structure unrelated to nearly all other opioid compounds.
substance.name: W-15

effects: The drug is marketed for its ability to suppress appetite and burn fat using higher dosages. The drug has a high ratio of caffeine and is reported to have anti-inflammatory properties.
substance.name: Yerba-mate

effects: Anadenanthera peregrina, also known as yopo, is a perennial tree native to the Caribbean and South America. It is an entheogen containing 5-MeO-DMT and DMT, and is used in healing ceremonies and rituals. The tree is also a source of dietary calcium.
substance.name: Yopo

effects: A substance that is structurally related to benzodiazepines. It is only used medically in veterinary medicine. It is usually used in tandem with either the potent NMDA antagonist tiletamine (at a 1:1 ratio) or with the α2 adrenergic receptor agonist xylazine. The drug is roughly around four times the potency of diazepam, yet is reportedly water soluable.
substance.name: Zolazepam

effects: Stimulant that is the homologue between α-PPP and α-PVP.
substance.name: Α-pbp

effects: β-Hydroxy-2C-B is a novel analogue of 2C-B that is a slightly less potent to 2C-B, and reportedly a longer duration. 2C-B is suspected to be the active metabolite of βk-2C-B.
substance.name: Βh-2c-b

effects: Extreme potency, 10-100x fentanyl. Naloxone may require multiple doses
substance.name: Nitazene

mechanismOfAction.summary: LSD prodrug — strained cyclobutane ring hydrolyzes to release LSD → 5-HT2A partial agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: N1-acyl LSD prodrug bearing a 1,2-dimethylcyclobutane-1-carbonyl group. The strained cyclobutane ring reportedly accelerates ester hydrolysis relative to most acyl-LSD prodrugs, producing faster onset (~20–30 min vs ~45–60 min for LSD). Pharmacological activity is attributed entirely to released LSD. Prodrug conversion t½ estimated ~3–4 h (not formally measured). All LSD-class risks apply: serotonin syndrome with MAOIs/SSRIs/lithium/tramadol, HPPD, full 5-HT2A cross-tolerance.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Presumed LSD prodrug via boronate ester hydrolysis → 5-HT2A partial agonist; boron toxicology completely unstudied.
mechanismOfAction.description: First boron-containing LSD prodrug (distinct from 1B-LSD which is 1-butanoyl-LSD). Boronate ester hydrolysis rate unknown; potency vs LSD empirically uncharacterized (mass-ratio claims of ≈100 µg LSD-equivalents are unvalidated). Emerged Dec 2025 as successor to banned 1S-LSD. Boron-specific toxicological profile is entirely unstudied.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Presumed LSD prodrug via sequential deethylation (→ 1Bz-LAE) then hydrolysis → LSD; full chain characterized in vitro only.
mechanismOfAction.description: N1-benzoyl LSD (benzoyl = aromatic acyl group; distinct from 1B-LSD which is 1-butanoyl). In vitro: deethylation to 1Bz-LAE confirmed (Azuma et al. 2026, Drug Test Anal); further hydrolysis to LSD presumed. No validated human potency or dose range established.

substance.name: DMNPC
effects: serotonin syndrome risk with serotonergic agents

mechanismOfAction.summary: Potent triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor (dopamine, norepinephrine and serotonin); ~2.5× cocaine potency at DAT. Piperidine-based phenyltropane/nocaine-related stimulant.
mechanismOfAction.description: Piperidine-based stimulant synthesized from arecoline. The 3S,4S enantiomer is most active; the 3R,4S enantiomer has the highest SERT selectivity. Acts by monoamine reuptake inhibition with no releasing-agent activity and no opioid receptor activity. No human pharmacological data. Significant serotonin syndrome risk in combination with MAOIs or other serotonergic agents.

substance.name: 3-Me-PCP
effects: more stimulating than ketamine per case reports

mechanismOfAction.summary: NMDA receptor antagonist (arylcyclohexylamine class); possible additional NE/DA reuptake inhibition inferred from structural analogues.
mechanismOfAction.description: Piperidine-substituted arylcyclohexylamine; 3-methyl substitution on the phenyl ring (meta). Confirmed NMDA antagonist by class pharmacology. Structurally distinct from 3-MeO-PCP (methoxy vs methyl) — do not transfer doses. First reported to UK forensic services. PCP-family dissociatives carry high psychosis/mania risk, bladder toxicity with chronic use, and dangerous respiratory depression with CNS depressants/opioids.

mechanismOfAction.summary: NMDA receptor antagonist (arylcyclohexylamine class); ethyl-substituted N-substituent vs piperidine ring of 3-Me-PCP.
mechanismOfAction.description: N-ethyl-substituted arylcyclohexylamine with 3-methyl phenyl ring substitution. NMDA antagonism confirmed by Wallach et al. 2015. Secondary pharmacology unstudied. First reported to EUDA March 2024. Structurally distinct from 3-MeO-PCE — do not transfer doses. Same arylcyclohexylamine risk profile as 3-Me-PCP.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Presumed NMDA receptor antagonist; 2-oxo-arylcyclohexylamine (methoxetamine/MXiPr relative with 2-fluoro substituent replacing 2-methoxy of MXE).
mechanismOfAction.description: Tentative IUPAC: 2-(2-fluorophenyl)-2-(isopropylamino)cyclohexan-1-one. The ortho-fluoro isomer replaces the methoxy group of MXE's pharmacophore. NMR-confirmed as ortho-F isomer. Sibling: 2-FXPr (n-propyl variant). Only a single anecdotal intranasal report exists (nervewing blog, 2025) — not a validated dose source; rapid tolerance noted in that report. No CAS/CID available.

substance.name: MPT
effects: Shulgin TiHKAL #34: inactive at ≤20 mg oral

mechanismOfAction.summary: Presumed 5-HT2A partial agonist (no published binding affinity data); may be inactive orally based on Shulgin self-trials.
mechanismOfAction.description: Substituted tryptamine; N-methyl, N-propyl disubstitution. Crystal structure solved (Chadeayne et al. 2019). Shulgin (TiHKAL #34) experienced no effect at oral doses up to 20 mg in self-trials; threshold listed as '>50 mg oral' with full dose ranges undocumented. Human psychedelic activity unconfirmed. Cross-tolerance with 5-HT2A psychedelics would be expected if psychedelic effects are confirmed.

mechanismOfAction.summary: N1-Boc thermolabile prodrug of 5-MeO-DALT; inactive until pyrolysis (~150–200°C) or acid conditions cleave the Boc group, releasing the 5-HT1A/2A agonist 5-MeO-DALT.
mechanismOfAction.description: 'NB-' prefix denotes N1-tert-butoxycarbonyl (NOT N-benzyl as sometimes assumed). Boc group cleaves at ~150–200°C (pyrolysis/smoking route) or under acid conditions. Parent 5-MeO-DALT: 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A agonist. Delivered parent dose from the Boc compound is unpredictable. No validated dosing for the Boc form itself. Parent 5-MeO-DALT oral: onset 10–15 min, total 2–4 h.

mechanismOfAction.summary: N1-Boc thermolabile prodrug of 5-MeO-MiPT ('moxy'); inactive until Boc cleavage releases the potent 5-HT1A/2A agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: 'NB-' prefix denotes N1-tert-butoxycarbonyl (NOT N-benzyl). Parent 5-MeO-MiPT: 5-HT1A Ki ~12–143 nM, 5-HT2A Ki ~113–449 nM (assay-dependent). Parent oral: onset 20–40 min, total 5–8 h, t½ ~2–3 h, CYP2D6 metabolism. Delivered parent dose from the Boc form is unpredictable. No validated dosing exists for the Boc compound.

substance.name: NBOC-DMT
effects: presumed DMT-class if Boc cleavage occurs

mechanismOfAction.summary: N1-Boc thermolabile prodrug of DMT; inactive until pyrolysis (~150–200 °C) or acid conditions cleave the Boc group, releasing DMT (5-HT2A agonist, σ1 ligand).
mechanismOfAction.description: 'NB-' prefix denotes N1-tert-butoxycarbonyl (NOT N-benzyl). The intact molecule is not itself active; the Boc group must be cleaved (pyrolysis/smoking or acid) to release DMT. Oral administration is inactive with or without an MAOI, because any absorbed intact compound must still be cleaved to DMT — claimed oral activity is unvalidated. Because the Boc-protected form is unscheduled, it is a common legal precursor form of DMT. No pharmacokinetic study or validated human dosing for the Boc compound.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Highly DAT-selective reuptake inhibitor (DAT IC50 = 7.6 nM); DAT/SERT selectivity ratio >40× cocaine → very high addiction and abuse potential.
mechanismOfAction.description: Synthetic cathinone, pyrovalerone subgroup (β-keto pyrrolidinophenone). Ortho ring-methyl isomer of α-PiHP. Peer-reviewed DAT IC50 = 7.6 nM (Forensic Sci Int 2025, PMID 40992254). NET not significantly inhibited. Documented in 113 Swedish seizures 2022–2025 and 5 forensic autopsy detections. No established human dose; strong 'no dose / high addiction potential' warning applies.

substance.name: bk-BZP
effects: dopamine and norepinephrine release (rodent data only)

mechanismOfAction.summary: DA/NE-releasing stimulant (piperazine class); mechanism based on rodent data only — human receptor binding data absent. NOT a cathinone despite the 'bk' prefix.
mechanismOfAction.description: 1-Benzoylpiperazine is a piperazine (benzoylpiperazine), not a cathinone. Despite the 'bk' (beta-keto) prefix, it lacks the beta-keto moiety characteristic of cathinones. Only rodent pharmacology available; no human receptor binding data confirmed.

substance.name: Bretazenil
effects: lower euphoria and abuse potential vs full agonists
can precipitate withdrawal in BZD-tolerant patients

mechanismOfAction.summary: Non-selective GABA-A BZD-site partial agonist (~35–58% intrinsic efficacy vs full agonist); wide therapeutic window with reduced tolerance/dependence potential compared to full agonists.
mechanismOfAction.description: Imidazo[1,2-a]-pyrrolo[2,3-d]-benzodiazepine; partial agonist at BZD binding site across α1–α6 subunit-containing GABA-A receptors (~35–58% maximal efficacy). Can precipitate withdrawal in BZD-tolerant users by occupying the site without full agonism. Never marketed. Potency: 0.5 mg ≈ 10 mg diazepam (psychomotor impairment studies). t½ ~2–4.5 h across multiple human PK studies.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Presumed high-potency GABA-A BZD-site positive allosteric modulator; loprazolam structural analog. Distinct from flualprazolam.
mechanismOfAction.description: Designer imidazobenzodiazepine; fluorinated analog of loprazolam (NOT flualprazolam — distinct compound). Described as 'very high potency' in NPS literature; no published Ki/EC50. Reported '1–2 mg' dosing is unsourced and unreliable. No validated human dosing data. Loprazolam t½ ~6–12 h — extrapolation to this compound is uncertain.

mechanismOfAction.summary: GABA-A positive allosteric modulator (triazolobenzodiazepine); in-silico QSAR suggests high potency. First described 1970s (Sternbach); never marketed.
mechanismOfAction.description: Triazolo-fused 1,4-benzodiazepine; enhances GABA-A chloride currents at the benzodiazepine site. In-silico QSAR indicates triazolobenzodiazepines are among the most potent BZD subclass. No published binding affinity data; no human pharmacokinetic data. First described by Sternbach in the 1970s; never developed or marketed.

mechanismOfAction.summary: α1(BZ1)-selective partial agonist at the GABA-A benzodiazepine binding site; triazolopyridazine scaffold (NOT a benzodiazepine structurally). Historical tool compound for dissecting α1-mediated sedation from α2-mediated anxiolysis.
mechanismOfAction.description: Triazolopyridazine (not a benzodiazepine). Historically used as a research tool to pharmacologically dissect α1 (BZ1)-mediated sedation/amnesia from α2 (BZ2)-mediated anxiolysis — preceding zolpidem as a selective α1 tool. Zolpidem-like selectivity profile but lower maximal efficacy (partial agonism). No human studies.

mechanismOfAction.summary: NE and DA releaser (amphetamine-like mechanism); milder stimulant profile than amphetamine with minimal serotonergic activity.
mechanismOfAction.description: Oxazolinone CNS stimulant/antidepressant developed by Lederle Laboratories in the 1960s. Mechanism: norepinephrine and dopamine release (amphetamine-like), minimal serotonergic activity. Clinical antidepressant effect demonstrated at ~40 mg/day in historical trials. Discontinued. DEA controlled substance status indicated by multiple secondary sources (exact schedule unconfirmed in primary DEA sources).

mechanismOfAction.summary: Sodium channel blocker (local anesthesia) + weaker DAT inhibitor than cocaine; tropane alkaloid naturally occurring in some Erythroxylum species.
mechanismOfAction.description: Descarbomethoxycocaine; pseudotropine benzoate. Na-channel block provides local anesthetic activity. DAT inhibition weaker than cocaine. Naturally occurs in some Erythroxylum species; documented as a street-cocaine cutting agent and contaminant. Ester structure → rapid hydrolysis by plasma esterases; short-acting. No formal human PK study. Cocaine analogue control applies in most jurisdictions.

substance.name: Emylcamate
effects: CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol/BZDs/opioids

mechanismOfAction.summary: Carbamate sedative-hypnotic; meprobamate-like GABAergic/barbiturate-like CNS depression with fast onset (carbamate chemical class). Mechanism incompletely characterized by modern GABA-A pharmacology.
mechanismOfAction.description: Carbamate ester anxiolytic and muscle relaxant developed by Merck (1961). Former brand names: Striatran, Striatal. Fast-onset CNS depression; meprobamate-class mechanism (GABAergic/barbiturate-like). Discontinued/obsolete. Additive CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol, benzodiazepines, and opioids. Overdose risk. Meprobamate-class control in many countries.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Sodium channel blocker (local anesthetic) + relatively potent monoamine transporter inhibition (DA/NE/5-HT reuptake) — stimulant properties distinguish it from purely local-anesthetic benzoates.
mechanismOfAction.description: Aminoester (benzoate) local anesthetic; dimethocaine-related (4-aminobenzoate scaffold). Historical dental anesthetic. Unlike purely local-anesthetic benzoates, meprylcaine also inhibits DA, NE, and 5-HT reuptake transporters, generating stimulant properties. Aminoester structure → rapid hydrolysis; short-acting. No recreational dose ranges established.

protocolDosing.notes: community physique dosing; no FDA-approved therapeutic dose; Phase I PK studied up to 100 mg single dose

mechanismOfAction.summary: Potent oral androgen receptor full agonist with tissue selectivity.
mechanismOfAction.description: Nonsteroidal SARM; binds AR with Ki ~7 nM; tissue-selective for muscle and bone over prostate; does not bind ERα/ERβ/PR/GR significantly; no aromatization. Long t½ (~44.7 h) leads to accumulation on daily dosing.

protocolDosing.notes: community/anecdotal; no human PK; claimed t½ ~48–60 h is unverified

mechanismOfAction.summary: Presumed AR agonist prodrug — benzoate ester hydrolysis releases RAD-140-like moiety.
mechanismOfAction.description: Nonsteroidal SARM; benzoate ester prodrug of a RAD-140 structural analog. Carboxylesterase hydrolysis presumed to yield active AR-agonist metabolite. No published receptor binding data for RAD-150 itself. Distinct molecule from RAD-140 (CAS 1208070-53-4 vs 1182367-47-0).

protocolDosing.notes: community/anecdotal; no human studies; t½ ~11.9 h from male rat data only — NOT validated in humans

mechanismOfAction.summary: High-affinity androgen receptor full agonist (Ki ~1.7 nM); tissue-selective SARM.
mechanismOfAction.description: Nonsteroidal SARM with among the highest AR affinity of characterized SARMs (Ki ~1.7 nM). Tissue-selective for muscle and bone. Investigated as male hormonal contraceptive in rodents due to spermatogenesis suppression. No human efficacy or safety data. t½ ~11.9 h is from male rat studies only.

substance.name: S4

protocolDosing.notes: split dosing required due to short t½ (~4–6 h); reversible yellow-tint vision risk increases at ≥50 mg/day

effects: reversible xanthopsia/yellow-tint vision (ocular AR binding, esp. ≥50 mg/day; resolves ~2–3 days post-cessation)

mechanismOfAction.summary: Oral androgen receptor partial agonist (Ki ~4 nM); tissue-selective; notable ocular AR binding.
mechanismOfAction.description: Nonsteroidal SARM; AR partial agonist with Ki ~4 nM; weaker androgenic activity at prostate vs full agonists. Critically binds ocular ARs causing reversible yellow-tint vision and night-vision impairment, especially at doses ≥50 mg/day. Short t½ (~4–6 h) requires split dosing.

protocolDosing.notes: community/anecdotal; no human studies; t½ ~6–12 h is unverified community claim; women use 0.5–2 mg/day

mechanismOfAction.summary: Steroidal SARM with dual mechanism: partial AR agonism plus functional myostatin inhibition via follistatin upregulation.
mechanismOfAction.description: 5α-DHT C17-methyl ester derivative; partial AR agonist (does not induce full N/C-terminal AR interaction unlike DHT) plus functional myostatin inhibitor via follistatin (FST) upregulation — the only characterized SARM with this dual mechanism. FST induction more potent than DHT in C2C12 myoblasts. CAS discrepancy: 1370003-76-1 confirmed by PubChem CID 119058028; 431579-34-9 is an unverified alternate.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Nonsteroidal AR partial agonist (Ki ~5 nM, ~64% DHT efficacy); anabolic:androgenic ratio ~2.45:1 in rat.
mechanismOfAction.description: Bicyclic azabicyclooctane scaffold SARM; AR partial agonist with EC50 ~1.58 nM in luciferase assay; selective over 47 other nuclear receptors at 10 µM. Never tested in humans — all data from rat studies. No published PK or t½ in any species.

protocolDosing.notes: community/anecdotal; no human studies; preclinical t½ ~4 h applies to preclinical route only; poor oral bioavailability in preclinical models

mechanismOfAction.summary: REV-ERBα/β agonist; represses Bmal1/Clock gene expression to alter circadian rhythms and metabolic gene programs.
mechanismOfAction.description: Nuclear receptor REV-ERB (NR1D1/NR1D2) agonist with EC50 ~790 nM REV-ERBα and ~560 nM REV-ERBβ. Represses clock gene Bmal1 expression; upregulates fatty acid oxidation genes; reduces inflammatory gene expression. Better oral bioavailability than SR9009. Human PK not established; t½ ~4 h is preclinical only.

substance.name: GW-501516

protocolDosing.notes: CARCINOGENICITY WARNING: multi-organ cancers in 2-year rodent studies at human-equivalent doses; GSK halted development 2007; WADA issued safety warning

effects: CRITICAL: multi-organ carcinogenicity in rodent studies (liver, stomach, bladder, skin, tongue, testes, ovaries)

mechanismOfAction.summary: Selective PPARδ agonist (EC50 ~1.2 nM); upregulates fatty acid oxidation genes and increases endurance. NOT a SARM.
mechanismOfAction.description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor delta (PPARδ/PPARβ) agonist; does not bind the androgen receptor. Upregulates genes for fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial biogenesis. Human PK is sparse — GSK discontinued development in 2007 due to multi-organ carcinogenicity in 2-year rodent studies at human-equivalent doses. WADA issued a specific safety warning.

protocolDosing.notes: 25 mg/day robustly elevates testosterone in trial data; used for PCT after AAS/SARM cycles; not FDA-approved (NDA failed 2013); compounding-pharmacy Rx

mechanismOfAction.summary: SERM; ER antagonist at hypothalamus/pituitary → disinhibition of LH/FSH secretion → increased endogenous testosterone.
mechanismOfAction.description: Trans-isomer (E-isomer) of clomiphene; blocks estrogen receptor at hypothalamus and pituitary, removing negative feedback and raising endogenous LH/FSH/testosterone. Differs from cis-isomer (zuclomiphene) which is a weak ER agonist. CYP2D6 metabolism; Tmax ~2–3 h; t½ ~10 h.

protocolDosing.notes: FDA-approved oncology dose is 2.5 mg once daily; physique/endocrine off-label micro-dosing 0.25–2.5 mg q2–3d is unvalidated patient-derived practice; t½ ~48 h → steady state at 2–6 weeks

mechanismOfAction.summary: Nonsteroidal (type II/triazole) aromatase inhibitor; competitive and reversible CYP19 inhibitor.
mechanismOfAction.description: Competitively and reversibly inhibits CYP19 (aromatase), reducing estradiol synthesis by 75–95% at 2.5 mg/day. No effect on adrenal steroidogenesis at therapeutic doses. Selectivity >10,000× for aromatase over other CYPs. FDA-approved for breast cancer. WADA S4.1 prohibited in sport. CYP3A4 and CYP2A6 metabolism.

substance.name: Tesofensine

protocolDosing.notes: t½ ~9 days (220 h) — significant accumulation; 2–3 weeks to steady state; 0.5 mg/day = ~10.6% placebo-corrected weight loss at 24 weeks; 1.0 mg dose abandoned (excess CV effects); approved in Mexico as Tesomet (with metoprolol)

effects: increased heart rate (dose-dependent, ~8 bpm at 0.5 mg)

mechanismOfAction.summary: Triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor (dopamine + norepinephrine + serotonin); phenyltropane scaffold.
mechanismOfAction.description: SNDRI; inhibits DAT, NET, and SERT → appetite suppression via hypothalamic circuits. Possible GLP-1 pathway potentiation. Active metabolite M1 via CYP3A4. t½ ~9 days (220 h) — extremely long, requires weeks to reach steady state; dose titration essential. Approved in Mexico as Tesomet (tesofensine + metoprolol 25 mg to offset HR increase). WADA S6 in-competition.

substance.name: Bemethyl

protocolDosing.notes: up to 750–1000 mg/day in some protocols; accumulates with repeated doses — course-based dosing with breaks manages this; human t½ not published; Russian pharmaceutical standard (Metaprot)

effects: increased physical/cognitive performance under hypoxic conditions (actoprotection)

mechanismOfAction.summary: Actoprotector/antihypoxant; activates genomic pathways increasing RNA synthesis and gluconeogenic enzyme induction.
mechanismOfAction.description: Benzimidazole actoprotector; activates PEPCK and G6Pase (gluconeogenic enzymes) via RNA synthesis induction; increases mitochondrial ATP production; antioxidant (reduces lipid peroxidation); antihypoxant (improves cellular oxygen utilization efficiency). BBB-penetrant. Accumulates with repeated doses — mechanism distinct from classical monoaminergic stimulants. Russian/CIS registered pharmaceutical (Metaprot); not FDA/EMA approved.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Pan-ERR agonist (ERRα/ERRβ/ERRγ); recruits PGC-1α → mitochondrial biogenesis and fatty acid oxidation.
mechanismOfAction.description: Small molecule pan-estrogen-related receptor agonist (ERRα EC50 ~98 nM, ERRβ ~230 nM, ERRγ ~430 nM); recruits PGC-1α coactivator to increase mitochondrial biogenesis, fatty acid oxidation, and OXPHOS gene expression. Increases Type IIa muscle fibers and exercise endurance in mice. ERRα-dependent mechanism confirmed by knockout. No human studies; poor drug-like properties (no published oral bioavailability in humans).

substance.name: RU58841

protocolDosing.notes: applied as ~1 mL of 5% solution to scalp; no completed human clinical trials; development abandoned by Roussel Uclaf/Hoechst; systemic t½ ~1 h (designed for rapid clearance)

effects: systemic AR antagonism risk at high topical absorption (gynecomastia, libido effects)

mechanismOfAction.summary: Topical nonsteroidal competitive AR antagonist; designed for scalp application with minimal systemic exposure.
mechanismOfAction.description: Competitive androgen receptor antagonist targeting scalp follicle ARs to block DHT-mediated miniaturization in androgenetic alopecia. Designed for minimal systemic absorption — rapid systemic clearance (t½ ~1 h parenteral) when absorbed, intentional design to reduce systemic antiandrogen effects. Development abandoned; no completed randomized controlled trials.

substance.name: Mirabegron

protocolDosing.notes: FDA-approved 25–50 mg for overactive bladder; metabolic/BAT research uses 200 mg (4× approved max) — substantial CV risk (≥20 bpm HR increase); CYP2D6 inhibitor at all doses (raises metoprolol, digoxin)

effects: bladder detrusor relaxation (FDA indication: overactive bladder)
increased brown adipose tissue thermogenesis (metabolic research, supratherapeutic dose)
mild heart rate increase at approved doses
significant heart rate and BP increase at 200 mg

mechanismOfAction.summary: Selective β3-adrenergic receptor agonist; bladder relaxation at approved doses; BAT thermogenesis at supratherapeutic doses.
mechanismOfAction.description: Selective β3-AR agonist (β1/β2 sparing at approved doses); FDA-approved for overactive bladder via bladder detrusor relaxation. Activates brown adipose tissue thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure at supratherapeutic doses (200 mg). Tmax ~3.5 h; oral bioavailability 29–35% (food-dependent). Moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — raises plasma levels of metoprolol, digoxin, and other CYP2D6 substrates.

substance.name: BAM-15
effects: increased energy expenditure without hyperthermia (mouse data)

mechanismOfAction.summary: Selective mitochondrial uncoupler; transports protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane without depolarizing the plasma membrane.
mechanismOfAction.description: Lipophilic weak acid protonophore; dissipates the inner mitochondrial membrane proton-motive force, increasing energy expenditure. Key distinction from DNP: does not depolarize the plasma membrane at therapeutic concentrations in mice, and does not raise body temperature. Mouse data: oral bioavailability ~67%, t½ ~1.7 h (oral gavage) or ~3 h (food admixture) in C57BL/6J mice. No human PK. Community dosing speculation is based on allometric scaling from mouse and is highly speculative.

protocolDosing.notes: no validated dosing — investigational (Phase 2), research/community protocol

mechanismOfAction.summary: Long-acting selective amylin (calcitonin/amylin) receptor agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: Proprietary acylated amylin analog under investigation for obesity; selective agonism of the amylin receptor promotes satiety and weight loss. Sequence unpublished.

protocolDosing.notes: blend/co-formulation of the amylin analog cagrilintide + the GLP-1 agonist semaglutide; investigational (Phase 3 REDEFINE). No validated standalone dosing — research/community protocol

mechanismOfAction.summary: Co-formulation: long-acting amylin analog (cagrilintide) + GLP-1 receptor agonist (semaglutide).
mechanismOfAction.description: Fixed-ratio combination of the amylin/calcitonin-receptor agonist cagrilintide and the GLP-1R agonist semaglutide, combining complementary satiety pathways for enhanced weight loss. Under Phase 3 evaluation (REDEFINE program).

protocolDosing.notes: no validated human dosing (primate studies only) — research/community protocol. NEPHROTOXIC: renal toxicity observed in primates

mechanismOfAction.summary: Pro-apoptotic peptidomimetic targeting white-fat vasculature.
mechanismOfAction.description: Homing peptide (CKGGRAKDC) fused via a GG linker to a pro-apoptotic D-amino-acid KLA domain [D(KLAKLAK)2]. Binds prohibitin/ANXA2 on white-adipose endothelium and induces apoptosis of the vasculature supplying fat tissue. Nephrotoxic.

protocolDosing.notes: community/research protocol; no validated human dosing. Hypoglycemia risk

mechanismOfAction.summary: Modified recombinant IGF-1 (83-aa analog) — IGF-1R agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: Human IGF-1 with an Arg3→Glu substitution and a 13-residue N-terminal extension that sharply reduce IGF-binding-protein affinity, increasing potency and duration. Agonism of IGF-1R drives anabolic hyperplasia/hypertrophy; hypoglycemia is a key risk.

protocolDosing.notes: community/research protocol; no validated human dosing. Localized potent action

mechanismOfAction.summary: Truncated IGF-1 (DES 1-3) — IGF-1R agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: Native IGF-1 lacking its first three N-terminal residues (Gly-Pro-Glu), giving ~10× lower IGF-binding-protein affinity and short, potent, localized action at IGF-1R.

protocolDosing.notes: trials ~1 mg/day oral/SC; community SC ~300 mcg/day. No validated approved dosing

mechanismOfAction.summary: Modified C-terminal HGH fragment — lipolytic, no growth effect.
mechanismOfAction.description: Tyr-hGH(177-191): the C-terminal lipolytic fragment of growth hormone with an added N-terminal Tyr. Stimulates lipolysis and inhibits lipogenesis via an HGH-fragment/β3-adrenergic pathway without raising IGF-1 or producing growth effects.

protocolDosing.notes: community/research protocol, fasted; no validated human dosing

mechanismOfAction.summary: C-terminal HGH fragment — lipolytic, no growth/IGF effect.
mechanismOfAction.description: hGH(176-191), a 15-residue C-terminal fragment of growth hormone (parent of AOD-9604 minus the added Tyr). Promotes lipolysis via a fat-cell β3 pathway without growth or IGF-1 effects.

protocolDosing.notes: intranasal community use (CIRS/mold-illness lore); no validated dosing. Very labile in solution

mechanismOfAction.summary: VPAC1/VPAC2 GPCR agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: 28-residue neuropeptide of the secretin/glucagon family. Agonism of the VPAC1 and VPAC2 G-protein-coupled receptors produces vasodilation, bronchodilation, immune modulation and neuroprotection.

protocolDosing.notes: no validated human dosing — research/community protocol

mechanismOfAction.summary: Casein-derived immunomodulatory hexapeptide.
mechanismOfAction.description: Bovine β-casein-derived hexapeptide (Pro-Gly-Pro-Ile-Pro-Asn) reported to have immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory/antitumor activity in preclinical studies.

protocolDosing.notes: no validated dosing — insufficient independent data; research/community protocol
popular co-administered healing stack: BPC-157 (~250–500 mcg/day) + TB-500 (~2–5 mg/week). Blend note referencing both; no validated human dosing

mechanismOfAction.summary: Co-administered tissue-repair stack (BPC-157 + Thymosin β4 fragment).
mechanismOfAction.description: Combination of the pentadecapeptide BPC-157 and the Thymosin β4 fragment TB-500, commonly stacked for soft-tissue and connective-tissue repair. Effects derive from each component's individual healing/angiogenic activity.

community 'PCT': single ~100 mcg SC off-label for LH/FSH stimulation

mechanismOfAction.summary: GnRH receptor superagonist (decapeptide, D-Trp6).
mechanismOfAction.description: GnRH agonist decapeptide with a D-Trp6 substitution. Produces an initial LH/FSH flare followed by receptor downregulation and gonadotropin suppression with continuous (depot) dosing.

protocolDosing.notes: intranasal research dose ~24 IU for social/CNS effects
obstetric IV titrated in mIU/min

mechanismOfAction.summary: Oxytocin receptor (OXTR) agonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: Cyclic nonapeptide neurohypophyseal hormone (disulfide-bridged, C-amide). OXTR agonism drives uterine contraction and milk letdown peripherally and, via intranasal delivery, social/bonding effects in the CNS.

protocolDosing.notes: no validated human dosing — potent μ-opioid (~30–40× morphine); respiratory depression risk. Research/community protocol only

mechanismOfAction.summary: Highly selective μ-opioid receptor agonist (heptapeptide, D-Ala2).
mechanismOfAction.description: Naturally occurring heptapeptide containing a D-Ala residue. Highly selective and potent μ-opioid receptor agonist (~30–40× morphine), with poor CNS penetration when given peripherally.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Semax-derived ACTH(4-7) analog; presumed BDNF/melanocortin nootropic.
mechanismOfAction.description: Poorly documented Semax derivative (variant of Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, likely acetylated/adamantyl-modified). Mechanism inferred from the Semax parent — BDNF upregulation and melanocortin-pathway signalling. No independent pharmacology published.

mechanismOfAction.summary: TREK-1 (K2P) potassium channel blocker; fast antidepressant candidate.
mechanismOfAction.description: Seven-residue fragment derived from spadin (sortilin/neurotensin-receptor-3 propeptide). Inhibits the TREK-1 background potassium channel, producing fast antidepressant-like and neurogenic effects in preclinical models.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Mitochondrial-derived peptide; cytoprotective and anti-apoptotic.
mechanismOfAction.description: 24-aa mitochondrial-derived peptide encoded in the 16S rRNA region. Binds Bax and IGFBP3 to inhibit apoptosis; exerts neuroprotective and metabolic effects. The [Gly14] analog (HNG) is markedly more potent.

protocolDosing.notes: trial dose; investigational, no approved regimen

mechanismOfAction.summary: Mitochondria-targeting tetrapeptide; binds cardiolipin to stabilize cristae.
mechanismOfAction.description: Cell-permeable tetrapeptide that concentrates on the inner mitochondrial membrane and binds cardiolipin, stabilizing cristae architecture, improving electron-transport efficiency, increasing ATP synthesis and reducing reactive oxygen species.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Senolytic D-retro-inverso peptide that disrupts FOXO4-p53 binding.
mechanismOfAction.description: FOXO4 DNA-binding-domain fragment synthesized as an all-D, reversed (D-retro-inverso) peptide fused to a TAT cell-penetrating sequence, conferring proteolytic resistance. Disrupts FOXO4-p53 interaction in senescent cells, causing p53 nuclear exclusion and selective apoptosis (senolysis). Renal-clearance concerns; mouse data only.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Membrane-disrupting anticancer peptide; p53(12-26) MDM2-binding domain plus penetratin leader.
mechanismOfAction.description: Fuses the p53 residues 12-26 (HDM-2/MDM2-binding domain) to a penetratin membrane-leader sequence. Selectively forms transmembrane pores in cancer cells that present HDM-2 at the membrane, causing necrosis while sparing normal cells. No human data.

hepatitis B/C and immune adjuvant; approved in ~35 countries (Zadaxin), not FDA-approved

mechanismOfAction.summary: Thymic immunomodulatory peptide; promotes T-cell maturation and Th1 responses.
mechanismOfAction.description: N-acetylated 28-aa thymic peptide that modulates T-cell maturation, increases Th1 cytokine output (IL-2, IFN), and enhances dendritic-cell and NK function.

mechanismOfAction.summary: SNAP-25 N-terminal mimic; inhibits SNARE complex to reduce muscle contraction ('topical Botox').
mechanismOfAction.description: Acetylated hexapeptide mimicking the N-terminus of SNAP-25. Competes for SNARE-complex assembly, attenuating catecholamine/acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction to soften expression lines.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Matrikine; stimulates collagen I/III and fibronectin synthesis.
mechanismOfAction.description: Palmitoylated pentapeptide (Pal-KTTKS) derived from a procollagen I fragment. Signals fibroblasts to upregulate collagen type I/III and fibronectin, improving dermal matrix.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Extended Argireline; competes with SNAP-25 in SNARE complex.
mechanismOfAction.description: Acetylated octapeptide that extends the Argireline motif, competing more strongly for SNAP-25 in the SNARE complex to reduce neuromuscular contraction.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Synthetic Waglerin-1 (snake-venom) mimic; nicotinic ACh receptor antagonist.
mechanismOfAction.description: Synthetic analog of Waglerin-1 from temple viper venom. Antagonizes the muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor at the neuromuscular junction, producing topical muscle relaxation.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Thrombospondin-1 mimic; activates latent TGF-β to increase collagen.
mechanismOfAction.description: Palmitoylated tripeptide (Pal-Lys-Val-Lys) mimicking thrombospondin-1's TGF-β-activating sequence. Converts latent TGF-β to its active form, stimulating dermal collagen synthesis.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Tubocurarine mimic; competitive acetylcholine-receptor antagonist at the NMJ.
mechanismOfAction.description: Pentapeptide acting as a curare-like competitive antagonist at the post-synaptic acetylcholine receptor of the neuromuscular junction, relaxing facial muscles topically.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Apo form of GHK-Cu; regenerative matrikine, collagen synthesis.
mechanismOfAction.description: The copper-free tripeptide Gly-His-Lys (apo form of GHK-Cu). Modulates wound-healing gene expression and stimulates collagen/glycosaminoglycan synthesis.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Copper peptide for hair-follicle stimulation.
mechanismOfAction.description: Ala-His-Lys copper(II) complex used topically on the scalp to promote dermal-papilla activity and follicle growth.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Matrikine; increases collagen and ECM synthesis.
mechanismOfAction.description: Palmitoylated Gly-His-Lys tripeptide. Acts as a matrikine signal to fibroblasts, upregulating collagen and extracellular-matrix components.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Palmitoylated AHK matrikine for topical anti-aging.
mechanismOfAction.description: Palmitoylated Ala-His-Lys tripeptide used topically as a matrikine for skin renewal and anti-aging.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Reduces IL-6; anti-inflammatory and anti-glycation matrikine.
mechanismOfAction.description: Palmitoylated Gly-Gln-Pro-Arg tetrapeptide that downregulates interleukin-6 release, reducing inflammatory and glycation-related skin damage.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Tyrosinase inhibitor; reduces melanin synthesis.
mechanismOfAction.description: Synthetic decapeptide that inhibits tyrosinase, the rate-limiting enzyme in melanogenesis, reducing hyperpigmentation.

mechanismOfAction.summary: MC1R antagonist; reduces melanin synthesis.
mechanismOfAction.description: Nine-residue peptide antagonizing the melanocortin-1 receptor, blocking α-MSH-driven melanogenesis to lighten skin.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Anti-aging matrikine.
mechanismOfAction.description: Palmitoylated dipeptide used topically as a matrikine signal for dermal renewal and anti-aging.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Enkephalin analog; modulates the enkephalin pathway for Botox-like muscle relaxation.
mechanismOfAction.description: Enkephalin-analog pentapeptide that engages the enkephalin signalling pathway at the neuromuscular junction to reduce muscle contraction and expression lines.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Collagen-fragment mimic; increases collagen synthesis.
mechanismOfAction.description: Synthetic collagen-fragment mimic (Gly-Pro-Hyp repeat type) that signals fibroblasts to increase collagen synthesis.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Activin/myostatin-binding glycoprotein isoform (circulating form).
mechanismOfAction.description: Follistatin splice isoform lacking the acidic C-terminal tail, predominantly circulating. Binds and neutralizes activin and myostatin (GDF-8), relieving inhibition of muscle growth. Human evidence is from AAV gene therapy, not injected peptide; injectable gray-market form has no human PK.

mechanismOfAction.summary: Activin/myostatin-binding glycoprotein isoform (cell-surface form).
mechanismOfAction.description: Follistatin splice isoform with the acidic C-terminal tail, associating with the cell surface/heparan sulfate. Binds and neutralizes activin and myostatin (GDF-8). Human evidence is from AAV gene therapy, not injected peptide; injectable gray-market form has no human PK.
